To prevent these silent failures, ingestion architectures must bind every recorded episode to an immutable calibration identifier and real-time clock synchronization metrics. Trajectories collected under conflicting geometric or temporal calibrations force neural policies to average incompatible sensorimotor distributions within identical state spaces.

::: {#fig-05-camera-calibration fig-env="figure" fig-pos="t" fig-cap="**Camera-to-robot calibration check on DROID scenes**: Randomly chosen DROID scenes with a robot mask rendered from the robot's URDF mesh at the recorded joint angles and projected through each camera's audited calibration, from the dataset's own post-hoc recalibration [@khazatsky2024droid]. Where the mask and the visible arm coincide, the extrinsics are consistent with the joint encoders; a displaced camera shows up as a mask that misses the arm, before any corrupted trajectory reaches the training pipeline. Source: Khazatsky et al., Fig. 13, CC BY 4.0." fig-alt="A seven-by-seven grid of darkened robot workspace photographs from many different rooms. In each, a colored silhouette of the robot arm, rendered from its kinematic model and recorded joint angles, is overlaid on the camera image."}
![](images/jpg/fig05_real_camera_calibration.jpg){width="95%"}
:::

### Sim-to-real transfer artifacts in rigid-body simulators {#sec-data-sim-to-real-artifacts}

Synthetic data generation replaces physical component wear with systematic modeling approximations. Consequently, degradation in synthetic datasets reflects numerical and kinematic assumptions within the simulation engine rather than sensor slippage or operator fatigue. Discrete-time physics engines resolve contact constraints once per integration step. The chosen mathematical formulation, whether strict complementarity constraints [@stewart1996implicit], convex soft-contact relaxations [@todorov2012mujoco], or penalty-based spring-damper models, determines penetration depths, frictional slip thresholds, and drivetrain compliance. While reinforcement learning agents actively exploit numerical quirks to maximize synthetic reward, behavioral cloning policies passively inherit them. Supervised imitation directly clones whatever unphysical contact impulses, penetrations, or frictionless transitions the simulator generates. Co-training on simulated and physical demonstrations can nonetheless substantially improve real-world policy success despite noticeable discrepancies between the two data regimes (@tbl-05-state-of-practice) [@maddukuri2025cotraining]. A physical ingestion pipeline cannot enforce perfect dynamic fidelity across arbitrary contact geometries; its core responsibility is maintaining end-to-end data provenance. Every synthetic trajectory must record its simulation engine, software version, contact solver parameters, and integration time step, while the scenario ledger explicitly identifies coverage cells populated exclusively by synthetic rollouts (@tbl-05-provenance-schema). Documenting these parameters enables downstream training and diagnostic pipelines to distinguish unphysical solver behavior from true hardware dynamics. Evaluating whether a simulator achieves sufficient fidelity for a specific manipulation task remains a training-time challenge: @sec-training-contact-exploit examines how relaxed contact formulations influence learned policy behavior.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ The decomposition of transfer discrepancies into dynamics, sensing, appearance, and timing channels, sized from paired command-response traces, is developed in @sec-training-sim-to-real-gap.
:::

### Rig-to-rig divergence across nominally identical fleets {#sec-data-fleet-divergence}

Beyond temporal drift on an isolated machine, two distinct failure modes emerge when demonstration pipelines aggregate data across multi-robot fleets: hardware divergence among nominally identical systems and the conflation of operational task failures with logging faults.

Hardware divergence manifests immediately when a secondary manipulator collects latching demonstrations intended for deployment across a fleet. Even among factory-identical robots of the same model number, individual units exhibit distinct gearbox backlash, thermal dissipation profiles, and motor controller filter tunings. For example, a newly commissioned arm may exhibit $0.02^\circ$ of backlash, whereas a heavily cycled arm displays $0.35^\circ$ of joint play accompanied by a $22\text{ ms}$ torque-response lag. Demonstrations recorded on the degraded arm embed aggressive lead compensation and high feedback gains to counteract deadband and phase delay; when replayed or imitated on the new arm, these aggressive actions induce severe limit-cycle oscillations. To protect fleet-wide models, data ingestion systems must bind a record of each unit's embodiment contract (its kinematic parameters, actuator serial numbers, controller firmware revisions, and identified dynamic models) to every recorded file, filtering out trajectories from hardware that violates the target platform's compatibility constraints.

The second hazard involves conflating physical execution failures with telemetry recording faults. A failed attempt represents a complete, physically valid sequence in which the robot attempted a task but failed to reach the objective. Discarding these episodes introduces severe survivorship bias[^fn-wald-survivorship-archive] and strips the dataset of the boundary states, recovery paths, and negative feedback signals needed to train stabilizing closed-loop policies. Conversely, a failed recording is an infrastructure defect, such as a dropped network packet, a corrupted image frame, or a circular buffer overrun. Ingesting a corrupted recording without explicit tracking presents missing or irregular sample intervals as a continuous, fixed-rate control stream, corrupting the policy's estimation of state derivatives. Data pipelines must therefore classify every session into one of three strict categories: a retained success, a retained physical failure, or an excluded logging fault annotated with diagnostic error codes. In a door-latching campaign, for instance, an episode halted by a contact-force tripwire constitutes a valid physical failure and remains in the provenance archive, whereas a run during which the 6-axis force-torque sensor dropped packets is quarantined with its associated bus error code. Retaining the failure does not admit its commands as expert imitation targets; only stabilized, reviewed recovery segments or expert-relabeled states qualify under the intervention curation rules.

[^fn-wald-survivorship-archive]: **Survivorship Bias**\index{Survivorship bias!Wald aircraft vulnerability}: During the Second World War, Abraham Wald of Columbia's Statistical Research Group estimated the vulnerability of combat aircraft from the damage on the planes that came back; the planes that were hit in the most vulnerable places were the ones missing from the sample [@mangel1984wald]. A demonstration archive filtered to successes has the same hole. The attempts that reached the failure boundary are exactly the ones absent, so the archive understates how often the boundary is reached and holds no states from it.

Hardware contracts can fail silently through unit mismatches that bypass traditional schema validators (war story \ref{ws-data-mars-climate-orbiter-unit-mismatch}).

::: {#ws-data-mars-climate-orbiter-unit-mismatch .callout-war-story title="Mars Climate Orbiter unit mismatch (1999)"}
**Context**: During its nine-month cruise to Mars in 1998 and 1999, the Mars Climate Orbiter fired small thrusters to desaturate its reaction wheels, and the navigation team on the ground folded the resulting velocity changes into the trajectory models used to plan each correction maneuver [@nasa1999mco].

**Mechanism**: A ground software file (called "Small Forces" in the investigation) reported thruster impulse in pound-force-seconds ($\text{lbf}\cdot\text{s}$), while the trajectory models that consumed it assumed newton-seconds ($\text{N}\cdot\text{s}$) as the interface specification required. Because $1\text{ lbf}\cdot\text{s} = 4.45\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$, every desaturation event entered the models too small by a factor of $4.45$. The values were well formed, in range, and of the expected type, so no schema check could flag them.

**Impact**: The accumulated error was never resolved during cruise. At orbit insertion the spacecraft passed about $57\text{ km}$ above the surface instead of the planned $226\text{ km}$ and was lost.

**Response**: The Mishap Investigation Board traced the loss to the missing unit conversion in the ground file and recommended that the Mars Polar Lander project verify consistent units throughout design and operations and audit all data transferred between JPL and Lockheed Martin Astronautics for compliance with the interface specification, along with stronger navigation review and anomaly escalation.

**Systems lesson**: A number carries its meaning only together with its units and its frame. A robot dataset runs the same risk on every action tap and every calibration. A record that stores a value without the units, frame, and calibration identifier it was produced under lets a mismatched rig pass every tensor check, which is why the provenance record of @sec-data-schema binds each tap to them.
:::

### Operational design domain blind spots and catastrophic interpolation {#sec-data-odd-blind-spots}

Encountering an unobserved operational state does not cause a learned neural controller to halt execution. Instead, the policy continues predicting control outputs, often executing familiar primitives in regimes where their physical prerequisites are completely violated. The `latch-recovery-02` demonstration archive described in @sec-data-intervention-recovery illustrates this vulnerability on the running machine. Its withdraw-and-reseat recovery behaviors were collected exclusively during low-speed guarded approaches at `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.v_guarded_str`. If contact occurs during the faster approach at `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.v_fast_str`, a regime documented as an unpopulated cell in the scenario ledger, the policy can naively select that same withdrawal motion. At elevated velocities, however, contact impulses and stored mechanical strain are substantially larger; attempting an unbraked withdrawal without first dissipating impact energy risks bending mechanical latch pins or damaging end-effector linkages. Operational safety demands that recovery primitives define explicit scenario ledger coverage for the physical states under which they execute, rather than merely logging the triggering failure conditions. Collection supplies experience, and closed-loop evaluation must establish competence in the conditions where the policy is to operate. A qualified permission restriction or physical constraint must exclude regimes that remain unsupported. The 2023 Cruise pullover recounted in @sec-boundary-when-fails is the same failure at road scale, in which a familiar maneuver, the pullover toward a minimal-risk condition, ran in a state no one had covered, with a pedestrian beneath the vehicle (war story \ref{ws-enforcement-cruise-fallback-dragging} gives the full account).

Sensor calibrations, human operator habits, actuator wear states, and operational design domain boundaries define the physical semantics of every recorded trajectory. If data ingestion pipelines strip these physical metadata to generate flat, uniform tensors, downstream evaluations cannot determine whether an autonomous failure stems from model capacity limitations or from unmodeled distribution shifts embedded within the training corpus. The structured provenance schema presented in @sec-data-schema establishes the formal architectural mechanisms required to preserve this physical context throughout dataset lifecycle operations.

## The Dataset Schema {#sec-data-schema}

Consider an audit of two trajectory files from the latch campaign, each holding the exact same number of state-action pairs logged at the same frequency. File A records trajectories from four authorized operators across several days, with no permission-path clamps and consistent fingertip pads throughout. File B records a single operator, logs 620 steps where safety logic clamped joint velocities, and spans an unannounced force-sensor re-zeroing midway through the session. A standard validation script checking only tensor dimensions and value ranges accepts both files without complaint. Yet treating them as interchangeable training data introduces silent, corrupting bugs. File B requires explicit intervention attribution and recalibration metadata before an engineer can interpret its action labels correctly. Furthermore, neither file's tensor geometry reveals which physical latch conditions the recorded data actually covers.

The dataset schema organizes the contextual evidence required to make ingestion decisions safely. It preserves the physical origin and timing of every signal, logs collection costs and dropouts, and documents which physical conditions the archive covers or omits. These fields reflect the mechanical and operational realities of the collection cell. While complete metadata cannot guarantee that a learned policy will operate successfully in closed loop, omitting it ensures that downstream pipelines will misinterpret physical signals.

The **provenance record**\index{Provenance record!definition}\index{Provenance record!physical AI contract} is the immutable, machine-readable artifact bound directly to a demonstration archive. It links every recorded trajectory to the specific plant, sensor calibrations, component wear state, four action taps, collection denominators, and scenario-ledger join ($\OccupiedLedgerCellCount / \RequiredLedgerCellCount$), including its count unit, eligibility and retention rule, and minimum, under which data collection occurred. Standard tensor shapes and training loss curves cannot validate a physical dataset. By recording an archive's empirical boundaries, the provenance record allows the policy manifest and the safety case to distinguish demonstrated historical experience from the operational competence that physical testing must establish. Datasheets for datasets [@gebru2021datasheets] standardize documentation for static corpora; embodied archives additionally require tracking physical wear, permission-path interventions, and tap histories across the causal boundary. Furthermore, this record must travel with the trajectory data itself. Because detachable sidecar files easily separate from their payloads during format conversions, engineers serialize the record as an immutable, hashed header within the container's root metadata, such as an MCAP top-level metadata record or a Zarr root attribute dictionary.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ The fifteen-record chain, in which the provenance record is the third record, is developed in @sec-appendix-systems-record-register.
:::

This schema establishes a direct lineage from low-level hardware characterization to policy training. It propagates the operating boundaries and thermal thresholds documented in the limit record, alongside the clock domains and jitter budgets established by the handoff record. The proposal boundary defines whose control authority each action tap reflects. During logging, the collection runtime appends unique plant identifiers, calibration matrices, mechanical wear metrics, yield denominators, and the scenario-ledger coverage join. This metadata establishes the recorded collection conditions and empirical coverage provided to the policy manifest, setting a baseline that subsequent evaluation suites test under closed-loop control.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↩ The handoff record, which extends each limit with the handoff and clock domain that locate it in the machine, is established in @sec-nervous-handoffs-matrix.
:::

Every trajectory admitted into the training corpus must identify its collection source, collector policy, and execution authority. For human teleoperation, the record logs the operator identifier, the interface hardware, and transport timing characteristics, for example a 6-DoF leader arm sampled at $100\text{ Hz}$ with $0.8\text{ ms}$ of input jitter. Storing an operator identifier, or capturing human faces on peripheral camera streams, makes an episode a record of people as well as of the robot. The schema therefore documents the legal and institutional basis under which each person was recorded, the authorized deployment purposes, and strict retention schedules. This governance ensures that an episode collected to teach latch insertion is not repurposed to evaluate the worker who demonstrated it. When data originates from an autonomous or mixed controller, the record stores the exact policy checkpoint, the planner version, and the active enforcement configuration, including Cartesian bounding boxes, joint velocity limits, and contact-force clamping thresholds. Trajectories must also record the active retention rule, documenting whether the runtime committed an episode automatically upon task completion, retained it after explicit operator review, or flagged it for inclusion as an instructive failure recovery.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ Purpose limits and retention schedules for records that capture people are enforced in @sec-release-recorded-people.
:::

A physical machine cannot be identified by a generic catalog name or model string. In real hardware, two nominally identical robot arms exhibit distinct mechanical behaviors due to manufacturing tolerances and component aging. The data record specifies the individual plant through its intrinsic and extrinsic sensor calibrations, embodiment contract (@sec-data-embodiment-contracts), motor drive firmware revisions, and component wear state. Replaceable contact surfaces alter the governing dynamics. A parallel gripper fitted with compliant silicone pads of Shore 30A hardness (a durometer scale for rubbers, on which higher numbers are stiffer) produces vastly different friction and compliance than the same mechanism fitted with worn Shore 60A polyurethane pads under identical joint commands. Maintenance milestones such as cable retensioning, drive belt replacements, gearbox swaps, and camera remounts are logged directly in the machine state record. If technicians recalibrated joint offsets between morning and afternoon collection shifts, the dataset must expose that boundary so downstream imitation learning does not attempt to resolve two conflicting kinematic mappings into a single policy.

Collection denominators reconcile every physical attempt as a retained success, a retained failure, or an excluded recording, while exposing the wall-clock time spent resetting the scene. Alongside those yield counts, the four action taps of @sec-data-four-stream-action-tap, override flags, and exclusion codes preserve the critical distinction between demonstrated behavior and permission-path intervention. When safety logic intervenes to clamp velocity or limit contact forces, the data pipeline must attribute those adjustments correctly rather than misinterpreting supervisory interventions as expert demonstrations.

The scenario join records dataset-supported cells (configurations containing retained demonstrations) and catalogues known absences where no empirical data exists. The ledger-policy digest binds the count unit, eligibility and retention rule, and declared minimum; when a minimum is specified, the record distinguishes occupied cells from those meeting it. Here, dataset support reflects historical logging coverage and must not be conflated with the evaluated support of a deployed policy. For the latch campaign, the record below connects collection cost to coverage; @tbl-05-provenance-schema maps its field groups to the decisions they support.

- **Denominators:** `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_raw_str` attempts per scheduled session at a net retention rate of `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.retention_str`, so `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` retained successful demonstrations cost `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_total_str` attempts over `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_sched_campaign_str` of scheduled cell time.
- **Retention rule:** an attempt whose contact force crosses the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.f_trip_str` tripwire triggers the qualified collection response and is kept as a labeled failure, outside the demonstration count, when its telemetry is valid; a recording that fails quality filtering is excluded with its exclusion code.
- **Scenario ledger:** plate offset (nominal, +`{python} LatchScenarioLedger.plate_offset_str`, −`{python} LatchScenarioLedger.plate_offset_str`) crossed with approach speed (`{python} LatchScenarioLedger.v_guarded_str`, `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.v_fast_str`), `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.n_cells_str` cells, held with the count and retention policy in the record as a digest rather than as a copy.
- **`supported_cells`:** the nominal plate at `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.v_guarded_str`, the only cell the original retained demonstrations occupy.
- **`known_absences`:** the other `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.n_zero_str` cells, every displaced plate and every approach at `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.v_fast_str`.

\Needspace{28\baselineskip}

| Provenance record           | Evidence retained                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Admission decision                                                                                  |
|:----------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Session**                 | Collector, operator, policy version, source type (physical, robot-free, or synthetic with generator and engine versions), collection mode (nominal, noise-injected, or gated intervention), sample rate, and timing jitter. | Check operator authorization and the session jitter budget.                                         |
| **Embodiment**              | Robot identity, geometry, gearing, backlash, firmware, and the redundancy parameter (elbow swivel angle or full joint vector).                                                                                              | Check reach, dynamics, and joint limits on the target plant.                                        |
| **Sensor calibration**      | Camera geometry, clock synchronization, and force/torque bias.                                                                                                                                                              | Check calibration age and timebase error.                                                           |
| **Contact wear**            | End-effector material, hardness, friction, flex cycles, and maintenance history.                                                                                                                                            | Revalidate contact data after material or compliance changes.                                       |
| **Four action taps**        | Requested, mapped, enforced, and measured values, each with its units and frame, plus override and clamp codes.                                                                                                             | Compare aligned values; attribute modified commands before choosing labels.                         |
| **Transition timing**       | Times of exposure midpoint, action issue, mapping, enforcement, response start, and response end, with clock IDs and synchronization errors.                                                                                | Check causal order and the declared response window.                                                |
| **Collection denominators** | Scheduled cell time, motion time, attempts, retained successes and failures, excluded recordings, and task configurations.                                                                                                  | Reconcile attempts against retained and excluded episodes.                                          |
| **Scenario support**        | Scenario-ledger and count-policy digest (unit, eligibility, retention, minimum), occupied cells, cells meeting any declared minimum, synthetic-only cells, and known absences.                                                                                                     | Identify collection gaps; require separate evidence for deployment claims.                          |
| **Consent and retention**   | People recorded (operator and any bystander in view), the consent or other basis for recording each, the declared purposes, the retention period, and who may read the record.                                              | Admit an episode only for a purpose its basis covers; delete or de-identify it when retention ends. |

: **Demonstration dataset provenance schema**: Evidence retained and the admission check applied to each field group of the provenance record; the embodiment, sensor calibration, and contact wear groups bind the individual plant that collected the data. {#tbl-05-provenance-schema tbl-colwidths="[24,38,38]"}

The policy manifest of @sec-training-policy-manifest cites each contributing archive by digest, including `latch-recovery-02` in the stipulated follow-up branch. The original record continues to describe the original campaign; new experience receives new provenance rather than rewriting old absences. Operator and override history also informs supervisory evaluation, while coverage and calibration evidence contributes to the release argument. Binding the metadata to the trajectory container helps preserve these relationships through ingestion, but cryptographic hashes do not automatically prevent misuse. Data loaders and ingestion pipelines must actively verify that trajectory arrays remain bound to their declared schema and calibration headers before training begins.

::: {.column-margin .margin-pointer}
↪ The release manifest, which binds this provenance record and its operating-domain coverage into the release argument, is developed in @sec-release-manifest.
:::

## Fallacies and Pitfalls {#sec-data-fallacies-pitfalls}

In pure software systems, data collection can often treat storage growth as an unvarnished positive: more web pages, text tokens, or labeled images generally broaden coverage. In physical artificial intelligence, however, datasets are tightly coupled to the mechanical dynamics, calibration state, and physical limits of the collection hardware. A dataset that passes every structural schema check, with zero dropped packets and consistent tensor dimensions, can still leave a deployed machine entirely blind to critical operational states. The operational distribution of physical data reflects three intertwined factors: the collecting policy (whether driven by human teleoperation or automated planning), the physical capabilities and wear of the collection rig, and the curation filters applied before admission to the archive. Neglecting these physical constraints leads to predictable engineering fallacies and costly operational pitfalls.

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Massive sample volume compensates for lack of operational state-space coverage.*

Surface-tracking tasks provide a clear illustration: suppose a manipulation policy must operate reliably across 500 distinct combinations of normal force, surface friction, and contact angle, but the archive covers only 45. Logging another collection run that adds $72{,}000$ control steps by repeating nominal trajectories through those same 45 states inflates the database, but it leaves physical coverage completely unchanged. High-frequency sampling in familiar regions merely records the same dynamic trajectory more densely, adding zero evidence about the unvisited friction regimes or steep contact angles. Ingestion pipelines that report massive data growth and zero dropped packets can create a false sense of security while leaving downstream policies brittle. A collection campaign earns its cost by addressing a declared coverage, label-quality, or evidence deficit. A populated cell may still need more or better demonstrations, while nominal repetition alone supplies no evidence about unvisited regimes.

**Architect's countermeasure:** Gate dataset admission on a support envelope relational join against an explicit scenario ledger, rather than step counts or raw byte volume. Require that new data collection campaigns specify which coverage, label-quality, or evidence deficit they target, and track scenario coverage ($\OccupiedLedgerCellCount / \RequiredLedgerCellCount$) as a primary engineering KPI alongside validation loss.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Assuming physical demonstration labels survive mechanical or contact hardware maintenance.*

Archived demonstrations do not retain physical validity when the underlying hardware changes, even if array shapes and data schemas remain identical. Consider what happens when a technician replaces a parallel gripper's compliant fingertips with stiffer pads and re-torques an adjacent camera bracket. The historical dataset still passes every automated pipeline check: sensor channels, array dimensions, and datatypes match expected specifications. If the camera bracket shifts, a known transformation matrix allows mathematical reprojection of visual coordinates. Contact mechanics, however, cannot be reprojected geometrically. The stiffer pads alter normal compliance and contact friction, causing grasp slip at substantially lower shear thresholds than the compliant material tolerated. Telemetry recorded before the swap captures the physical behavior of an obsolete body; training a closed-loop force controller on those historical tactile profiles will cause grasping failures on the modified hardware. Data provenance must track the full mechanical and calibration state of the collection rig so that any hardware alteration immediately triggers targeted review and recollected baselines.

**Architect's countermeasure:** Bind every trajectory file to an immutable hardware state hash that captures camera extrinsics, motor serial numbers, and contact surface material specifications. When maintenance events alter contact stiffness or camera mountings, invalidate historical tactile and force labels for that cell until an automated revalidation protocol verifies dynamic equivalence.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Filtering out aborted safety interventions to sanitize the demonstration dataset.*

Purging aborted demonstrations to produce a flawless training set introduces severe survivorship bias into physical policies.\index{Survivorship bias!in physical datasets} Consider an automated peg-insertion pipeline spanning 1,000 recorded attempts. Of these, 180 runs triggered a safety cutoff when contact forces reached or exceeded a $15.0\text{ N}$ trip threshold, leaving 820 nominal runs that succeeded with an 82 percent yield. A curation script discards the 180 aborted and recovery episodes, preserving only the smooth runs where forces stayed comfortably below $8.0\text{ N}$. When deployed in production, minor surface misalignment inevitably pushes an insertion force to $9.5\text{ N}$. Although this force remains below the $15.0\text{ N}$ trip threshold, the policy encounters a state completely outside its training support. Because the sanitization script erased every observation between nominal tracking and failure, the archive supplies no supervision for these near-boundary dynamics, so recovery behavior remains unsupported. Pruning near-boundary and intervention data strips away the exact state-action pairs the policy needs to regain stability after a disturbance.

**Architect's countermeasure:** Implement three-way intervention curation at data ingestion. Quarantine learner commands between divergence ($\DivergenceInstant$) and takeover ($\TakeoverInstant$) for safety auditing only, preserve the visited boundary states for expert relabeling via corrective aggregation (DAgger), and admit the subsequent human recovery as an expert sequence only after the operator's measured stabilization ($\OperatorStabilizationInstant$), masking the blend and re-orientation that precede it.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Pitfall**: *Merging demonstrations collected across kinematically asymmetric leader interfaces.*

Merging trajectories across disparate teleoperation input interfaces can quietly bake kinematic dead zones into the dataset.\index{Teleoperation!kinematic asymmetry} Suppose two operators collect snap-fit assembly demonstrations using different leader devices to puppet identical follower arms. The first leader mechanism features detented wrist mechanics that restrict roll to two discrete positions ($\LeaderWristRollAngle \in \{0.0^\circ, 90.0^\circ\}$). The second leader uses a continuous gimbal that mechanically limits roll travel to $[-15.0^\circ, +15.0^\circ]$. Merging the two collections yields 4,000 episodes and increases overall sample volume, but neither interface can express orientations between $20.0^\circ$ and $70.0^\circ$. Even though the follower arm can navigate that full range, the combined archive contains zero training targets within this $50.0^\circ$ gap. Aggregating heterogeneous inputs cannot fill gaps that neither device can mechanically traverse. Downstream imitation policies trained on the combined dataset will fail whenever initial conditions or part tolerances demand intermediate orientations.

**Architect's countermeasure:** Apply the cross-embodiment compatibility contract to the leader interface itself, checking before recording that the leader and follower share the required reachable poses, joint motion ranges, and ability to move in the required directions. Enforce continuous orientation coverage checks across task-space degrees of freedom during data QA to detect mechanical dead-zones.

:::

::: {.fallacy-pitfall}

**Fallacy**: *Physical data collection scales linearly with labor hours just like internet scraping scales with compute.*\index{Data collection!linear scaling fallacy}

Treating physical data collection as an easily parallelized, linear process like web scraping ignores the mechanical entropy and human fatigue inherent to physical experimentation.\index{Data collection!linear scaling fallacy} Teams often extrapolate campaign timelines from early pilot runs, for example by projecting that an initial pace of 50 successful episodes per operator-hour will scale linearly across weeks of shifts. In reality, continuous operation degrades both hardware and teleoperator consistency. Repetitive contact impacts cause backlash and tooth wear in strain-wave gearboxes, thermal expansion and sensor drift cause uncalibrated joint encoders to drift away from physical ground truth, and human fatigue introduces latency spikes and jerky trajectories. As wear accumulates, the proportion of episodes passing quality filtering steadily drops, even while scheduled labor hours remain constant. Pilot runs conducted on pristine hardware systematically overstate long-term collection yield. Campaign planning must budget for routine recalibration, mechanical maintenance, ergonomic rests, and discarded runs alongside raw operator hours.

**Architect's countermeasure:** Budget collection campaigns in net validated demonstration yield ($\UsableDemonstrationYield = \lfloor \ActiveMotionDuration / \AttemptCycleDuration \rfloor \cdot \DemonstrationRetentionRate$) and component fatigue cycles ($\RatedFatigueLife$ ratings for strain-wave gears and internal flex harnesses), rather than gross scheduled operator hours. Estimate the overhead multiplier from the campaign's calibration, reset, retention, and rest assumptions; validate it against sustained collection yield.

:::

## Summary {#sec-data-summary}

A physical machine manufactures its own training data, so every record carries the loop that produced it: the operator's request, the permission path's admission, and the body's response, all under the machine's current calibration and wear. Collecting that data is costly in a way scraping is not. In the latch campaign, only `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.yield_pct_str` of each scheduled hour survives as retained demonstration motion once startup, calibration, operator rest, resets, failed attempts, and quality filtering are paid for, and the wrist's flex cable consumes the larger fraction of its assumed fatigue rating. Because every attempt spends cell time and component life whether or not it is kept, and because correlated control steps hold few independent samples, a campaign earns its cost by addressing a declared coverage, label-quality, or evidence deficit, including inadequate evidence within a populated cell.

Which states the archive holds is a question the archive cannot answer about itself. Coverage is a join between empirical occupancy and a scenario ledger derived from the declared operational design domain, and against the ledger the door actually demands, the baseline latch archive fills one cell of `{python} LatchScenarioLedger.n_cells_str`. Inside even a populated cell, a cloned policy's first error carries it off the demonstrated corridor into states where nothing in the archive constrains its output, which is why behavioral cloning's worst-case cost grows with the square of the horizon. Interventions supply the missing learner-visited states, but only after curation at the divergence, takeover, and stabilization timestamps separates the learner's commands from the expert's recovery. Aggregating expert labels on those states makes the worst-case cost linear in the horizon only while the recoverability constant stays bounded; where a mistake cannot be undone, the state belongs to the permission path, not to the dataset.

A label is only as meaningful as the tap, clock, and plant behind it. Imitating the request teaches commands the permission path would have clamped, imitating the measured response teaches compliance and backlash as intent, and pairing either with a misdated frame converts timing error into position error at the speed of the motion. Range normalization cannot carry a label to another embodiment, and a bumped camera bracket or worn pad silently changes what a stored tuple means. The provenance record binds each archive to its taps, timestamps, plant, calibration, collection denominators, and known absences, so that training and evaluation can tell demonstrated experience from evaluated competence.

@Tbl-05-key-equations summarizes the load-bearing equations introduced throughout this chapter, detailing the physical boundaries each expression defines, the architectural decisions it governs, and its formal derivation.

| Equation                                                                                                                                                                                              | What it bounds or decides                                                                                                                                                             | Derived in                     |
|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| $\ExpectedTaskCostSum(\pi)-\ExpectedTaskCostSum(\pi^*) \le \BehaviorCloningHorizon^2\SingleStepImitationError$                                                                                        | The worst-case excess cost of cloning on expert states under a 0–1 action loss; the bound becomes uninformative once $\SingleStepImitationError > 1/\BehaviorCloningHorizon$          | @eq-data-quadratic-drift       |
| $\ExpectedTaskCostSum(\AggregationLearnedPolicy) \le \ExpectedTaskCostSum(\pi^*) + \DeviationDisadvantage\,\BehaviorCloningHorizon\,\AggregatedSurrogateLoss + \mathcal{O}(1)$                        | The cost after aggregating expert labels on learner-visited states, linear in $\BehaviorCloningHorizon$ only while the recoverability constant $\DeviationDisadvantage$ stays bounded | @eq-data-dagger-bound          |
| $\EffectiveSampleSize = \RawRecordCount(1-\SerialAutocorrelation)/(1+\SerialAutocorrelation)$                                                                                                         | The effective number of independent observations contained in a serially correlated telemetry stream for a single statistic                                                           | @eq-data-effective-sample-size |
| $\SyncPairingDisplacement \approx \Velocity\,\ObservationPairingLag$                                                                                                                                  | The spatial error introduced by inter-sensor pairing latency, defining the maximum allowable delay for a specified task clearance                                                     | @eq-data-sync-displacement     |
| $\RollingShutterFrameSkew = (\ImageHeight - 1)\,\RollingShutterRowReadout$                                                                                                                            | The temporal skew across a rolling-shutter frame, which end-effector motion translates into geometric image distortion                                                                | @eq-data-rolling-shutter-skew  |
| $\TeleoperationRoundTripLatency = \DisplayPipelineLatency + \OperatorResponseLatency + \TeleoperationCommandLatency + \FollowerMechanicalLatency$                                                     | The round-trip phase lag in teleoperation between an observed state and the physical execution of the human correction                                                                | @eq-data-teleop-loop-latency   |
| $\UsableDemonstrationYield = \lfloor \ActiveMotionDuration/\AttemptCycleDuration \rfloor \DemonstrationRetentionRate$                                                                                 | The yield of usable demonstrations per scheduled session, determining the cell time and mechanical wear required for a campaign target                                                | @eq-data-demonstration-yield   |
| $\EstimatedDivergenceInstant$: first threshold crossing, when captured, in $[\TakeoverInstant - \PreTriggerWindowDuration,\, \TakeoverInstant]$                                                       | The estimated onset of trajectory drift before human takeover, determining whether the lookback window captures the causal error                                                      | @eq-data-divergence-point      |
| $\ReprojectionResidual = \lVert \ObservedPixelCoordinates - \operatorname{proj}_{\CameraIntrinsicCalibrationMatrix}(\BaseToCameraTransform\,\ForwardKinematicsMap(\GeneralizedCoordinates)) \rVert_2$ | The extrinsic reprojection residual used to verify that camera calibration remains aligned with kinematic joint encoders                                                              | @eq-data-reprojection-residual |

: **Key equations of physical data**: Each load-bearing equation of the chapter, the limit it bounds or the decision it settles, and the equation where it is derived. {#tbl-05-key-equations tbl-colwidths="[40,42,18]"}

::: {.callout-takeaways title="Physical data collection and provenance"}
* **Coverage measures distinct physical configurations rather than sample volume:** Repeated nominal trajectories add millions of telemetry rows without expanding scenario coverage. Adjacent control steps are so strongly autocorrelated that an hour of permission-tick records holds only about `{python} EffectiveSampleSize.n_eff_str` independent samples for a slowly varying statistic, and even independent samples support only the cells where they land. An engineering team must measure dataset completeness by joining logged trajectories against an explicit scenario ledger that spans the operational design domain, rather than relying on raw row counts or the archive's own observed extremes.
* **Offline validation loss cannot detect coverage deficits:** Because conventional train-validation splits sample from the same underlying trajectory distribution, a policy can exhibit near-zero validation loss while leaving critical operational cells completely unvisited. Only auditing the dataset against an independent scenario ledger reveals these silent omissions before deployment.
* **Every action tap represents a distinct physical control signal:** An operator's commanded request, the resolved kinematic setpoint, the safety-filtered actuator command, and the measured joint response diverge whenever hardware limiters, friction, or permission guards intervene. Logging each tap alongside synchronized timestamps ensures the supervisory target remains causal and preserves unambiguous evidence of physical interventions.
* **Preserve aborted runs and interventions with rigorous causal attribution:** Discarding failed attempts discards the most valuable boundary-adjacent states in the operational envelope. Autonomous commands preceding a human takeover must be archived for fault analysis and counterfactual relabeling rather than misattributed as expert demonstrations, while the subsequent corrective maneuver should be reviewed, trimmed, and stored as an explicit recovery trajectory.
* **Physical telemetry remains bound to specific hardware embodiments:** While optical perspectives can be reprojected across camera geometries, dynamic properties such as joint friction, structural compliance, and gearbox backlash are embedded directly into recorded force and torque signals. Simple range normalization masks these physical discrepancies without resolving them, requiring thorough re-calibration and verification whenever data is transferred across hardware platforms.
* **Targeted recovery data broadens operational competence under new provenance:** An immutable dataset records the boundary conditions of a specific collection campaign, but engineers can systematically expand policy capabilities by appending verified recovery sequences under separate provenance tags. Asserting an expanded operational claim, however, requires end-to-end closed-loop validation on the physical machine under those target conditions.
:::

Each latch archive in this chapter ended the same way, with a short list of supported cells and a longer list of known absences. That ratio is not a defect of one campaign. It is what the second law, endogenous data (principle \ref{pri-vol4-endogenous-drift}), costs in practice. A machine whose actions choose its next states can only record the states its collecting policy chose, and every additional state it records is paid for in cell time and component life. The known absences in the provenance record are the price list. They say which experience the machine never bought, and therefore which claims no amount of training on this archive can support.

Read that way, the engineering question shifts from how much data a campaign collected to which absences it retired and what each one cost. The displaced-plate cell that `latch-recovery-02` fills moves from the absence list to the supported list under new provenance. The faster approach, which no one collected, stays on the list, and the permission path must keep refusing it until evidence arrives.

## Historical Perspective and Further Reading {#sec-data-history}

Demonstration in robotics began not as data collection for machine learning, but as teleoperation for hazardous environments. At Argonne National Laboratory, Raymond Goertz developed mechanically coupled master-slave manipulators to handle radioactive materials behind heavy shielding [@goertz1949master]. These early systems linked the operator's handle directly to remote mechanical tongs through cables and counterweights; because the transmission was entirely mechanical, contact forces against objects reflected instantly and passively back to the operator's hand.

The systems challenge shifted radically when electrical servos and digital communication networks replaced mechanical linkages. Introducing transmission latency into the bilateral loop between the operator interface and the actuated follower can inject artificial energy into the feedback channel, quickly driving the coupled system into violent instability. @anderson1989bilateral proved that even small transmission delays can destabilize a bilateral teleoperator and established a framework that preserves delayed-channel passivity under its constant-delay model. Stability of the complete loop also depends on the connected systems and their interconnection conditions. @niemeyer1991stable reformulated this remedy through wave variables, transforming power variables (force and velocity) into traveling wave representations that behave as passive transmission lines under the constant-delay model. In their comprehensive survey, @hokayem2006bilateral trace the progression from Goertz's early linkages to modern delay-robust control schemes. Every teleoperation data-collection interface operates under the fundamental compromise illuminated by these works: balancing faithful haptic transparency against the conditions needed to preserve passivity. The physical trajectories, contact transitions, and actuation commands captured in an embodied training archive inherently reflect the compromises of the collection hardware.

Synthesizing feedback controllers directly from recorded demonstrations followed an equally grounded trajectory. In one of the earliest end-to-end vision-based driving systems, ALVINN mapped camera frames to steering angles for an autonomous van [@pomerleau1989alvinn; @pomerleau1991efficient]. ALVINN immediately ran into the recovery gap: because expert drivers kept the van centered within the lane, the recorded dataset contained virtually no examples of drifting off course or recovering from road shoulders. Pomerleau resolved this issue through an early form of data augmentation, synthetically warping camera images and computing the corresponding corrective steering angles to teach the network how to return to the road center.

As the field matured, @argall2009survey unified robot learning from demonstration into a comprehensive framework, formalizing how data collection modalities dictate policy representations and analyzing the kinematic correspondence problem between the demonstrator and the physical robot. The theoretical mechanics of compounding execution errors were established by @ross2010efficient, who proved that naive behavioral cloning yields an error bound that grows quadratically with the task horizon ($\CovariateDriftBound$) under covariate shift. To escape this quadratic penalty, @ross2011reduction introduced Dataset Aggregation (DAgger), demonstrating that rolling out the learner while querying the expert along the induced state distribution achieves an optimal linear bound ($\mathcal{O}(\BehaviorCloningHorizon\SingleStepImitationError)$), provided the environment satisfies a finite recoverability condition. Practical robotics deployments adapted this theoretical machinery to human supervisors who cannot label millions of counterfactual query states. Human-gated DAgger [@kelly2019hgdagger] transferred control to a human expert only during critical trajectory deviations, while DART [@laskey2017dart] injected continuous stochastic noise into the actuators during teleoperation to force human demonstrators to execute recovery maneuvers naturally. The empirical intervention strategies and recovery curation workflows in @sec-data-intervention-recovery trace directly to these foundational methods.

The accounting of state-space coverage and sampling validity borrows from older statistical and control foundations. @bellman1957dynamic named the curse of dimensionality to describe the exponential explosion of discrete state spaces in dynamic programming. In environmental time series, climatologists demonstrated that serially correlated records dramatically reduce the effective degrees of freedom, requiring explicit adjustments to compute true sample sizes [@thiebaux1984interpretation]. Simultaneously, Abraham Wald's wartime analysis of returning aircraft showed that evaluating only surviving samples systematically blinds the observer to critical failure modes [@mangel1984wald].

Robot learning confronted all three phenomena as datasets evolved from isolated laboratory demonstrations into massive multi-robot corpora [@walke2023bridgedata; @khazatsky2024droid; @open_x_embodiment_collaboration2024open]. While cross-institution pooling supplies visual and environmental variations that no single robotic cell can generate, it also aggregates heterogeneous actuator dynamics, unmodeled camera latencies, and latent operator selection biases. Standardizing such corpora requires both an explicit compatibility contract across kinematics and a rigorous accounting of unobserved conditions. Although dataset documentation frameworks [@gebru2021datasheets] originally addressed provenance and social biases in digital corpora, physical robotics demands tracking hardware-level ground truths. The physical dataset schema and provenance architecture detailed in @sec-data-schema extend these documentation principles to capture actuator tap points, calibration matrices, dynamic delays, and known boundary omissions.

The following readings chart the progression from classical bilateral teleoperation to modern pooled robot corpora:

- @hokayem2006bilateral provides an exhaustive survey of bilateral teleoperation control, charting the historical transition from mechanically coupled manipulators to passivity-based and wave-variable architectures. It explains the core control-theoretic tension between transparent force reflection and robust stability when non-negligible communication delays separate the operator from the robot.
- @pomerleau1991efficient presents a compact, highly practical diagnosis of the recovery gap and compounding errors in end-to-end behavioral cloning. The paper details how synthetic visual transformations of road images generated corrective training labels, demonstrating the necessity of off-trajectory recovery data decades before formal distribution-shift theory was codified.
- @argall2009survey synthesizes robot learning from demonstration into a foundational taxonomy based on demonstration collection mechanisms and policy derivation techniques. It highlights the correspondence problem across differing human and robotic kinematic structures, which @sec-data-cross-embodiment formalizes as a strict cross-embodiment mapping contract.
- @ross2011reduction introduces the Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) algorithm and establishes the formal reduction of imitation learning to online convex optimization. It proves that querying an expert along the learner's visited trajectory distribution converts the quadratic error growth of behavioral cloning into a linear bound, defining the critical recoverability constant presented in @eq-data-dagger-bound.
- @open_x_embodiment_collaboration2024open documents the Open X-Embodiment initiative, pooling over one million trajectories across dozens of robot platforms and institutions. The paper is essential reading for systems engineers, illustrating both the positive transfer enabled by scale and the severe architectural challenges of normalizing disparate action spaces, sampling rates, and sensor configurations.
- @gebru2021datasheets establishes the foundational methodology for documenting dataset motivation, composition, collection workflows, and intended use. Contrasting this general framework with @tbl-05-provenance-schema clarifies the specialized physical, electrical, and dynamical metadata required to safely train and deploy embodied controllers.

## Problems {#sec-data-problems}

```{python}
#| label: calc-data-problems
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ GIVENS FOR THE END-OF-CHAPTER PROBLEMS (LEGO)
# ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# │ Context: @sec-data-problems.
# │ Goal:    Hold the givens the problems add to the chapter's cells: the
# │          compute module's memory, the navigation camera's readout time,
# │          an illustrative wrist-camera geometry for reprojection, an
# │          illustrative takeover trace, a chosen per-cell requirement, and
# │          the transfer source (a bimanual leader-follower arm cell).
# │          Answers are not printed; the private solution script computes them.
# │ Show:    64 GiB; 16.6 ms; 900 px, 0.60 m, 3 mm, 0.5 deg, 1.5 px; drift
# │          window = design out-of-loop takeover; 1.5 s and 6.0 s after takeover;
# │          2 s short lookback; N_min = 50; ALOHA 14 DoF at 50 Hz, 0.5 kg.
# │ How:     Registry reads (RM, AISLE, Embodied.Manipulator); other givens are
# │          labeled illustrative or chosen in the problem text.
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from mlsysim import *
from mlsysim.core.units import *
from mlsysim.fmt import fmt, fmt_int, fmt_memory_capacity, fmt_latency, fmt_length, fmt_frequency, fmt_mass, fmt_time, check

RM = Embodied.MobileManipulator.WarehouseMobileManipulator
AISLE = Embodied.Scenario.WarehouseAisle

class DataProblems:
    """Givens that the chapter's problems add beyond the worked examples."""

    # ┌── 1. LOAD (Constants & Parameters) ─────────────────────────────────
    soc_mem = RM.brain_soc.memory.capacity  # category: datasheet
    nav_readout = RM.nav_camera.readout_time  # category: datasheet
    f_px = 900.0  # wrist-camera focal length in pixels; category: illustrative
    z_work = 0.60 * meter  # camera-to-gripper working distance; category: illustrative
    shift = 3.0 * millimeter  # bracket shift, as in @sec-data-plant-drift; category: illustrative
    tilt_deg = 0.5  # bracket tilt in degrees, as in @sec-data-plant-drift; category: illustrative
    thresh_px = 1.5  # session reprojection threshold; category: illustrative
    t_drift = AISLE.t_takeover_out_of_loop  # category: derived (sourced p90 take-over time + transport)
    t_stab = 1.5 * second  # stabilization after takeover; category: illustrative
    t_rec = 6.0 * second  # latch release after takeover; category: illustrative
    lookback_short = 2.0 * second  # category: illustrative
    servo = RM.permission_rate  # category: datasheet
    n_min = 50  # retained demonstrations per ledger cell; category: chosen
    src = Embodied.Manipulator.ALOHA_Bimanual  # category: literature
    arm = RM.arm  # category: datasheet

    # ┌── 2. EXECUTE (Compute) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
    lookback = AISLE.pre_trigger_window
    reproj_shift = f_px * (shift / z_work).to("").magnitude  # checked, not printed

    # ┌── 3. GUARD (Invariants) ───────────────────────────────────────────
    check(
        RM.nav_camera.shutter_type == "rolling" and RM.wrist_camera.shutter_type == "global",
        "Problem 3 assumes a rolling navigation camera and a global-shutter wrist camera",
    )
    check(t_drift < lookback, "Problem 7: the drift window must fit the design lookback")
    check(t_drift > lookback_short, "Problem 7: the short lookback must lose the divergence point")
    check(t_rec > t_stab, "Recovery must end after stabilization")
    check(reproj_shift > thresh_px, "Problem 6: the 3 mm shift must exceed the threshold")
    check(n_min > DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_usable, "Problem 8: one cell should need more than one session")
    check(src.control_frequency < servo and src.dofs != arm.dofs, "Problem 9 needs a slower, topologically different source")

    # ┌── 4. OUTPUT (Formatting) ──────────────────────────────────────────
    soc_mem_str = fmt_memory_capacity(soc_mem, unit=GiB, precision=0)
    nav_readout_str = fmt_latency(nav_readout, unit=millisecond, precision=1)
    f_px_str = fmt_int(int(f_px))
    z_work_str = fmt_length(z_work, unit=meter, precision=2)
    shift_str = fmt_length(shift, unit=millimeter, precision=0)
    tilt_str = fmt(tilt_deg, precision=1)
    thresh_str = fmt(thresh_px, precision=1)
    t_drift_str = fmt_time(t_drift, unit=second, precision=3)
    t_stab_str = fmt_time(t_stab, unit=second, precision=1)
    t_rec_str = fmt_time(t_rec, unit=second, precision=0)
    lookback_short_str = fmt_time(lookback_short, unit=second, precision=0)
    servo_str = fmt_frequency(servo, unit=ureg.kilohertz, precision=0)
    n_min_str = fmt_int(n_min)
    src_dofs_str = fmt_int(src.dofs)
    src_rate_str = fmt_frequency(src.control_frequency, precision=0)
    src_payload_str = fmt_mass(src.payload_capacity, unit=kilogram, precision=1)
    arm_dofs_str = fmt_int(arm.dofs)
    arm_payload_str = fmt_mass(arm.payload_capacity, unit=kilogram, precision=0)
```

The problems below build on the physical parameters, timing budgets, and hardware specifications established across this chapter's worked examples. Where physical measurements have not yet been logged on the physical machine, illustrative parameters stand in as baseline engineering assumptions. Each problem centers on a concrete operational decision. The bracketed tags specify the analytical mode (direct computation, systems design, or architectural critique) along with the corresponding learning objectives (LO) assessed.

1. **[Compute, LO3] The reset tax.** In the collection session analyzed in notebook \ref{nbk-data-flex-cable-ceiling}, installing a faster re-latch fixture would halve the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_rst_str` reset duration, whereas an improved strike-plate guide would halve the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.failure_pct_str` in-trial failure rate. For each modification independently, use @eq-data-demonstration-yield to recompute the total attempts required per session, the scheduled cell occupancy time to collect `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` retained demonstrations, and the percentage of rated flex-cable fatigue life consumed by the campaign. Determine which investment to prioritize when cell time binds, and which to fund when flex-cable fatigue binds.
2. **[Compute, LO5] Sizing the pre-trigger buffer.** The real-time logger described in @sec-data-intervention-recovery must maintain a `{python} DataLookbackWindow.t_lookback_str` lookback window. Calculate the required buffer capacity across three configurations: for the kinematic stream alone (`{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.bytes_per_step_str` bytes per step logged at `{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.f_log_str`), for all sensor streams combined at the raw `{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.bw_total_str` bandwidth of notebook \ref{nbk-data-ingestion-bandwidth-storage-budgets-multi-camera}, and for the complete session compressed to `{python} MultiCameraIngestionBudget.bw_compressed_str`. Compare each memory footprint against the `{python} DataProblems.soc_mem_str` physical memory of the onboard compute module, and decide which streams belong in the locked, pre-allocated ring buffer.
3. **[Compute, LO2] Rolling shutter at the latch.** The navigation camera reads out its sensor rows over `{python} DataProblems.nav_readout_str` (datasheet specification), whereas the wrist camera uses a global shutter that exposes every row simultaneously. Modeling this row readout as the full-frame skew in @eq-data-rolling-shutter-skew, determine the physical displacement across one navigation frame at the `{python} SyncDisplacement.v_transit_str` transit velocity and at both latch approach speeds. Compare each resulting displacement against the latch mechanism's `{python} SyncDisplacement.clearance_str` clearance, and calculate the maximum approach speed at which raw navigation frames can serve directly as latch observations without requiring row-time timestamp corrections.
4. **[Compute, LO1] Effective samples in the latch archive.** Apply @eq-data-effective-sample-size with autocorrelation parameter $\SerialAutocorrelation =$ `{python} EffectiveSampleSize.rho_str` to the `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` retained demonstrations, each lasting `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_att_str` and recorded at `{python} EffectiveSampleSize.f_log_str`. Treat the selected scalar statistic as stationary with the stated autoregressive correlation and the same mean and variance within each episode, and treat separate episodes as independent. Use the chapter's large-sample approximation for each episode and sum those episode estimates; finite episode boundaries limit its accuracy. Compare four metrics for the campaign: raw record count, effective sample size, total episode count, and the fraction of the latch scenario ledger covered, as charted in @fig-05-collector-coverage-ledger. Explain which metric fundamentally limits what a trained policy can accomplish when encountering a displaced strike plate, and why the other three metrics fail to expose that limitation.
5. **[Compute, LO1] When the bound says nothing.** A single latch attempt lasts `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_att_str`. Assuming the `{python} BoundComparison.f_ctrl_str` control rate used in the comparison following @eq-data-dagger-bound, calculate the discrete horizon $\BehaviorCloningHorizon$, the per-step imitation error threshold above which the compounding error bound in @eq-data-quadratic-drift becomes vacuous, and the numerical value of both bounds at $\SingleStepImitationError =$ `{python} BoundComparison.eps_str` with recovery parameter $\DeviationDisadvantage = 1$. Explain why the training loss $\AggregatedSurrogateLoss$ differs fundamentally from the true policy error $\SingleStepImitationError$, and analyze how the bound comparison behaves if $\DeviationDisadvantage$ grows proportionally with $\BehaviorCloningHorizon$.
6. **[Compute, LO7] A bumped bracket in pixels.** A wrist camera with a focal length of `{python} DataProblems.f_px_str` px observes the gripper at a working distance of `{python} DataProblems.z_work_str`. Using the pinhole camera model from @sec-data-plant-drift, estimate the reprojection residual (@eq-data-reprojection-residual) produced by a `{python} DataProblems.shift_str` lateral bracket shift, and separately by a `{python} DataProblems.tilt_str`° angular tilt. For these estimates, place the observed point initially on the optical axis, translate the camera perpendicular to that axis for the lateral shift, and rotate it about its optical center around an axis perpendicular to the viewing direction for the tilt; neglect distortion and other calibration errors. Given a session diagnostic threshold that flags residuals exceeding `{python} DataProblems.thresh_str` px, find the smallest lateral shift this check can detect. Decide whether this automated gate reliably catches a calibration misalignment as large as the latch's `{python} SyncDisplacement.clearance_str` mechanical clearance.
7. **[Design, LO5] Curating an intervention episode.** In an illustrative `latch-recovery-02` trial, the gripper's lateral error crosses the tolerance threshold $\DivergenceTolerance$ one design out-of-loop takeover duration, `{python} DataProblems.t_drift_str`, before the human operator overrides autonomous control at $\TakeoverInstant$. The operator stabilizes the arm `{python} DataProblems.t_stab_str` after taking control, and the latch releases `{python} DataProblems.t_rec_str` after the takeover event. The system logger samples at `{python} DataProblems.servo_str`, while the learning policy issues commands at `{python} BoundComparison.f_ctrl_str`. Map the segmentation intervals from @fig-05-compounding-error-flywheel onto this timeline, calculate the number of logged states eligible for expert action relabeling, determine how many autonomous learner commands must be masked out, and give the duration of the admitted expert recovery trajectory. Verify whether the drift window fits within the `{python} DataLookbackWindow.t_lookback_str` lookback buffer. Finally, identify what information a truncated `{python} DataProblems.lookback_short_str` lookback loses, and specify how the curation pipeline must handle the resulting episode.
8. **[Design, LO4] A pad-wear axis.** Expand the scenario coverage ledger of @fig-05-collector-coverage-ledger by adding a pad-wear axis (distinguishing between new and worn gripper pads), setting a target coverage requirement of $\MinimumCellSupportCount =$ `{python} DataProblems.n_min_str` retained demonstrations per cell. Assuming the baseline campaign operated exclusively with new pads, catalog the occupied cells and documented absences for both the initial archive and its `latch-recovery-02` successor. Distinguish occupancy from meeting the retained-demonstration minimum; mark successor count sufficiency as unknown wherever counts are not supplied. Using the retained demonstration yield per session derived in notebook \ref{nbk-data-flex-cable-ceiling}, calculate the number of physical sessions needed to populate one empty cell to $\MinimumCellSupportCount$. Propose an execution plan for the subsequent data collection campaign, identifying which operating cells must remain protected within the deterministic permission envelope rather than targeted for autonomous collection.
9. **[Design, LO6] Borrowing from a bimanual arm cell.** An engineering team proposes incorporating door-opening demonstrations collected on a bimanual leader-follower teleoperation station (`{python} DataProblems.src_dofs_str` degrees of freedom across two arms and their grippers, commanded at `{python} DataProblems.src_rate_str`, with a `{python} DataProblems.src_payload_str` payload capacity) into the mobile manipulator's latch dataset. The target robot features a single arm with `{python} DataProblems.arm_dofs_str` joints, a `{python} DataProblems.arm_payload_str` payload capacity, and a `{python} DataProblems.servo_str` permission tick rate. Determine which architectural compatibility gate from @sec-data-kinematic-topology these source demonstrations must satisfy for self-supervised representation pretraining vs. direct supervised action labeling. When generating target labels, identify an action representation that can transfer across these embodiments, determine what the target's inverse kinematics solver must infer that the teleoperation setup never captured, and calculate the source system's zero-order hold lag (half the command period, as shown in @sec-appendix-control-zoh). Identify the target command-period information needed for the comparison without substituting its permission tick. Finally, state what evidence would let the target-label gate admit, relabel, or reject the approach, contact, and latch-release segments of the source trajectories.
10. **[Design, LO8] The successor's provenance record.** Construct the full dataset provenance record for the `latch-recovery-02` release, completing every field group in @tbl-05-provenance-schema with explicit values from this chapter or marking unmeasured entries as *to be measured*. Explain how its supported cells and known absences contrast with those of the baseline archive, specify what entries must populate its collection-mode and intervention fields under the filtering protocols of @sec-data-intervention-recovery, and describe how the schema establishes verifiable lineage back to the parent archive without mutating historical records.
11. **[Critique, LO1, LO4] A large archive with a small loss.** A team presents the conservative demonstration archive from @tbl-data-collector-coverage-ledger, citing its low validation loss on held-out trajectories as evidence that the policy is ready for autonomous contact tasks. Critique this readiness claim. Identify precisely what distribution the validation loss evaluates, compute the fraction of the operational scenario grid actually populated by the archive, and analyze which absence mechanisms from @sec-data-intervention-recovery account for the unpopulated cells. Formulate three essential questions the team must answer before deploying the policy to autonomous hardware, specifying the empirical evidence required for each answer.
12. **[Critique, LO3, LO7] A plan budgeted in demonstration time.** A data-collection proposal budgets `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` latch demonstrations by estimating active teleoperation time as `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.n_target_str` $\times$ `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_att_str`, scheduling only a single camera calibration at the start of the campaign. Critique this operational plan against the fatigue and cell scheduling model in notebook \ref{nbk-data-flex-cable-ceiling}. Compute the planned demonstration time, the actual scheduled cell time demanded by the illustrative session parameters, and the ratio between the two. Identify the physical wear mechanisms that this budget neglects. Then determine which structural and environmental drift modes go undetected by an initial calibration across `{python} DemonstrationYieldFatigue.t_sched_campaign_str` of operational cell time, and outline the periodic verification routines the team must add (@sec-data-plant-drift).

::: {.callout-chapter-connection title="From demonstrations to policies"}
What does a policy learn from an archive whose provenance record lists more absences than supported cells? It learns the supported cells, and its training score gives no sign of where the absences begin. The baseline latch archive covers only the nominal strike plate at the guarded approach, and @sec-training opens with two candidates built on it: `latch-bc-01`, cloned from those demonstrations, and `latch-sim-02`, distilled from a simulator teacher that learned the fast approach no one collected on the machine. Each improves in training while hiding a dependency the hardware will expose. The chapter then carries the curated `latch-recovery-02` archive into a recovery candidate and writes each candidate's evidence into a policy manifest whose declared operating domain cannot exceed the cells its provenance supports. @Sec-evaluation then tests whether that declared domain holds on the machine.
:::
